policies.sentence: Using AI to do the work undermines learning, understanding and retention of skills.
AI use or reliance hinders students' own critical, creative and independent thinking.
Learning comes from doing the work yourself: practice, effort, debugging and working through problems.
The course is designed to build students' own skills, understanding and independent problem-solving.
The course's AI restrictions exist to protect learning, original thought and authentic understanding.
AI can solve homework, gives too much help, and hands over others' solutions.
Outsourcing homework to AI gains students nothing and gives no incentive.
Students should use AI to assist and complement their learning and effort, not replace it.
Students should do the work and the thinking themselves rather than outsource it to AI.
Students must not use AI in ways that replace their own learning or growth.
Students must not use generative AI on homework.
Students must spend time practicing and take responsibility for learning from the work.
